summary.format: Faithful raster crops and archival photographs; no new vector reconstruction

pacific-great-eastern-railway.notes: Ten historical PGE logo illustrations recovered from Greg M. Kennelly’s January 1991 Cariboo article, alongside two original brochure crops. Reproduction dates and historical-use dates are recorded separately; several equipment, corporate and advertising marks overlapped. An archival circa-1970 equipment photograph adds the BC-map herald.

bc-railway-company.notes: The 1972 dogwood identity is represented by a 1991 newsletter masthead reproduction. The continuing provincial company, its 1984 operating subsidiary and CN’s 2004 operating-business acquisition are distinguished in the sourced railway history. The current BC Railway Company website wordmark remains a separate specimen.

assets.label: PGE early caribou equipment herald
assets.publisher: The Cariboo; Greg M. Kennelly (logo article and livery diagrams)
assets.creator: Greg M. Kennelly; illustration from Will Whittaker’s 1946 photograph of caboose 1802
assets.sourceLocator: The Cariboo, Issue 3, January 1991, PDF page 7
assets.historicalDateLabel: Introduced in the second quarter of 1945; altered by mid-1946
assets.dateNote: January 1991 dates the reproduced illustration in this newsletter, not the historical mark’s introduction. Introduced in the second quarter of 1945; altered by mid-1946. New mikado locomotive deliveries reported by author; image based on 1946 photograph.
assets.notes: Locomotives, cabooses and some passenger cars, including gas car 102. Both right- and left-facing versions existed; the head usually faced forwards, with exceptions. 42/21-inch outer/inner diameter on locomotives/cabooses; 24/14-inch on passenger cars. The author lists Mikados 57, 160 and 161. The illustration is one reproduction, not proof all applications used identical proportions.

assets.historicalDateLabel: Lettering introduced between 31 May and 26 September 1948; corporate timetable use until 19 January 1966
assets.dateNote: January 1991 dates the reproduced illustration in this newsletter, not the historical mark’s introduction. Lettering introduced between 31 May and 26 September 1948; corporate timetable use until 19 January 1966. Bounded interval between cited public timetables.
assets.notes: Public timetable front and back covers; business-car tail signs exception. Front-cover use generally continued until 7 June 1964, except timetables 73C and 73L. Initials then replaced the caribou on front covers; caribou remained on back covers until the BC map mark took over on 19 January 1966. These dates concern corporate timetable applications, not universal withdrawal from equipment.
